Welcome to **Health Informatics in Python** — a tutorial series for health informatics professionals, clinical data scientists, and graduate students who want to work with health data as it actually exists: coded, standardized, exchanged, governed, and reused.

Health informatics is the discipline concerned with how health information is **captured, structured, stored, exchanged, and used**. This series starts with that infrastructure — EHRs, terminologies, HL7/FHIR, OMOP — and then applies Python to privacy, clinical text, decision support, claims, warehousing, bulk data, and emerging AI.

**Modules:** 4 parts · 16 notebooks  
**Level:** Beginner through advanced · healthcare or public-health background helpful  
**Language:** Python 3.10+ · Jupyter-compatible  
**Dataset:** Synthetic throughout · no real patients  
**Author:** Dr. Zia U. Ahmed · [Upatta Analytics](https://github.com/zia207)

## Why Health Informatics in Python?

Analytics is only as good as the data infrastructure feeding it. **This series focuses on the informatics layer that most analytics courses skip:**

1. **Representation first** — ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, CPT, and FHIR resources are treated as data types, not footnotes.
2. **Systems that talk to each other** — ingestion, ETL, OMOP CDM, data quality, and bulk FHIR are the path from a hospital system to an analysis-ready table.
3. **Use with care** — de-identification, clinical NLP, decision support, claims, and warehousing are shown as applied informatics, not isolated algorithms.

## Series Architecture

The sixteen modules form four parts. Work through them in order, or jump to a part that matches your role.

| Part | Modules | Focus |
|------|---------|-------|
| **I — Foundations** | 01–04 | What informatics is · health data types · clinical terminologies · standards and formats |
| **II — Interoperability & Data Engineering** | 05–08 | FHIR in depth · ingestion and ETL · OMOP CDM · data quality |
| **III — Privacy, Text & Applied Informatics** | 09–11 | De-identification and governance · clinical NLP · clinical decision support |
| **IV — Advanced Topics** | 12–16 | Public health · claims · data warehousing · bulk data · emerging AI |

Each module follows a consistent arc: **concepts → Python demonstration → interpretation**.

## Getting Started

1. Browse notebooks using the **sidebar** on the left — modules are organised by part.
2. Clone the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/zia207/Health-informatics) to run notebooks locally or in Jupyter.
3. Start with [Module 01 · What Health Informatics Is](Notebooks/Part I - Foundations (Beginner)/01_what_is_health_informatics.ipynb) for the mental model of the series.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zia207/Health-informatics.git
cd Health-informatics
jupyter lab
```

## Who Is This For?

> Health informatics professionals, clinical data scientists, public health analysts, and graduate students who want to understand how health data is structured, exchanged, and governed — and then work with it in Python.

If you already know Python and want prediction, causal inference, or geospatial epidemiology, see [Health Analytics with Python](https://zia207.github.io/Health-Analytics-with-Python/).
